issues.title: [BugFix] Fix embedding fine-grained TP hang and first-request corruption under DP > 1
issues.body:
## Problem

`finegrained_tp_config.embedding_tensor_parallel_size > 1` under DP > 1 — where idle DP engines execute dummy batches — fails in three ways (reproduced with DP4×TP4/EP16 + dspark speculative decoding on Atlas 900 A3):

1. **First-request hang**: idle DP engines' dummy batches feed `inputs_embeds` directly and skip the main model's token-embedding lookup, so the cross-DP exchange inside `AscendVocabParallelEmbedding` has no counterpart on the idle ranks. The busy ranks' `all_gather`/`reduce_scatter` never complete and the engine dies after the HCCL execution timeout once the first real request arrives.
2. **HCCL EI0019 / collective deadlock / first-request corruption**: the exchange group's HCCL communicator is created lazily on the first collective. When that first exchange lands on the request path, the concurrent communicator creation races across ranks (HCCL EI0019 endpoint collisions) or deadlocks inside the collective; in the raced case the first exchange itself returns corrupted data and the very first request decodes garbage from its first prefill token.
3. **Draft embeddings desync the exchange group**: the vocab plan builder routed every `embed_tokens` module FINE_GRAINED, including speculative-decoding draft models. Drafts are fed `inputs_embeds` during propose replay (or looked up outside the paired exchange steps), so their first call desynchronizes the cross-DP exchange group, and their weights get sharded over a group whose collectives they never join.

Issue 1 is a pre-existing gap (the embedding knob had never actually been exercised with idle DP engines), not a regression. Issues 1 and 3 only affect models whose (dummy) batches feed `inputs_embeds` — multimodal-input and prompt-embeds models; text models' dummy batches carry input_ids, run the embedding exchange inside the dummy forward, and already self-pair across DP ranks.

## Fixes

| Commit | Location | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Join | `vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py` (`execute_model`) | **Embedding dummy join**, mirroring the existing LM-head join: on a dummy (non-profile) step of an inputs-embeds model, every rank that owns the exchange-group embedding joins the exchange once with zero token ids at the group-agreed `embedding_tp_capacity`, so all ranks contribute the same exchange length per step |
| Draft exclusion | `vllm_ascend/ops/vocab_parallel_embedding.py` (plan builder) | The fine-grained embedding plan is restricted to main-model modules; draft-model embeddings fall back to the standard TP layout |
| Warmup | `vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py` (`load_model`) | One capacity-sized exchange right after weight loading (after the NZ/early-kernel warmup threads join) eagerly builds the HCCL communicator before any traffic |

The join is gated on the runner's `uses_inputs_embeds` (multimodal inputs or prompt embeds): only those models feed `inputs_embeds` in dummy batches and skip the embedding lookup. Text models' dummy batches carry input_ids, so the dummy forward already runs the exchange at capacity and self-pairs — a runner-side join there would double the idle side's contribution (2 vs the busy side's 1 per step) and break a previously working pairing.

### Why the model-tag signal for draft exclusion

The draft loading paths (the `draft_model` proposer, the DSpark/EAGLE/DFlash speculators, extract-hidden-states) construct their models **without any distinguishing module prefix** — a DSpark draft's `model.embed_tokens` is indistinguishable from a text main model's by prefix. All of them run inside a `set_model_tag` context whose tag differs from the default `"backbone"` used while the main model is built, so resolving the construction-time model tag is the reliable main-vs-draft signal. Main-model embeddings of every naming convention (`model.embed_tokens`, `language_model.model.embed_tokens`, ...) keep the fine-grained plan; a main model that builds its embedding inside a non-backbone tag context falls back to the standard layout (noted in the docstring).

## Performance notes

- Busy ranks' real steps only pay a boolean short-circuit (`dummy_run` is checked first); the join/warmup are fully behind `embedding_tp_enable()`, so deployments without the knob are unaffected.
- The idle-side join joins the *same* collective the busy ranks' real exchange participates in (same module, group, capacity) — it adds no second collective and the per-step fabric traffic equals the all-busy baseline. Its local cost (capacity-sized lookup + reduce-scatter) is well under the dummy forward itself, and smaller than the existing LM-head join that runs in the same scenario.
- The warmup is one-time at load (communicator creation plus one capacity-sized exchange), negligible against model loading.
- Memory: with `tensor_parallel_size > 1` a draft's embedding table keeps the same vocab/tp per-rank size as before (only the sharding axis changes). With `tensor_parallel_size == 1`, a draft that owns its full table now replicates it per rank instead of sharding it over the exchange group (e.g. ~0.7 GiB/rank for a 152k×3072 bf16 table) — documented in `Fine_grained_TP.md`.

## Testing

- New unit tests cover all three fixes: plan-level draft exclusion under `draft_model`/`dspark_head`/`eagle_head` tags, the capacity-sized zero-id dummy join (parametrized over the knob and `uses_inputs_embeds`, pinning that text models do not join), the absence of a join for real runs, and the load-time warmup. `tests/ut/ops`, `tests/ut/worker` and `tests/ut/distributed` pass with results identical to the base commit on the vLLM commit paired with this main HEAD (verified on an A3 server container with torch_npu, comparing failure sets against the pristine base).
- The three mechanisms were validated end-to-end on the equivalent downstream implementation (`releases/v0.30.0rc2`): 16-NPU Atlas 900 A3, DP4×TP4/EP16, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-W8A8 + dspark (7-token, greedy), `embedding_tp=4` stacked with `lmhead_tp=4` — cudagraph FULL_DECODE_ONLY and eager both 11/11 chat requests correct including the first cold request after startup, 0 ERROR in logs; disabling the dummy join reproduces the first-request HCCL timeout, confirming the join is required. An E2E rerun of this exact main-based branch is planned.

## Relation to #19841

Independent: this PR does not depend on the lmhead/embedding compose enhancement in #19841 and stands on its own on current main. That PR should carry these three fixes when it lands.

## Follow-up

V2 is the default model runner on Ascend, but a feature list still falls back to V1 (pooling, VL encoder graph, `draft_model`-style spec decode, ngram/suffix, dflash2 graph, p-eagle); the v1 runner has neither the embedding dummy join nor the warmup, and its fine-grained embedding TP under idle DP engines remains broken there. The v1 equivalents are left as a follow-up (the plan-builder fix is shared and already applies to V1).

issues.title: [Feature][Kimi] Provision the shared draft embedding on the last PP stage
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

[RFC #21537](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/21537) PR 1 of 3: make the target responsible for providing the shared input embedding on its last pipeline-parallel stage.

Under PP, a DSpark draft that reuses the target input embedding runs on the last stage, where the target embedding is normally a `PPMissingLayer`. This PR provisions a real `VocabParallelEmbedding` there during `AscendKimiLinearModel` construction; the normal target checkpoint loader fills the TP shard, the upstream sharing check aliases the loaded module into the draft, and a successful unrotated share is flagged so the post-load `align_draft_weights` step keeps the shared shard instead of reloading a private copy over it.

Changes by file:

- `vllm_ascend/models/kimi_k3/kimi_k3.py` — the `_draft_needs_target_embed` provisioning predicate (dspark method + `uses_target_hidden_states` gate, `K3DSparkModel` exclusion for the MLA draft's checkpoint-owned embedding, over-vocab exclusion matching the draft-side loader's share condition, QuaRot exclusion) and the relaxed allocation condition in the constructor. The predicate asks "must this stage create the shard the draft will alias" — a consumption question that upstream `spec_decode_needs_target_embed` (which only answers "may the draft use the target embedding") does not cover.
- `vllm_ascend/models/qwen3_dspark.py` — an explicit class-level `has_own_embed_tokens = False` on `AscendQwen3DSparkForCausalLM`, mirroring every other upstream drafter declaration. `SupportsEagleBase` already provides the attribute through the Qwen3 MRO, so this is a convention alignment that also guards against upstream MRO changes.
- `vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_dspark.py` — `_make_pp_safe_maybe_share_target_embed(mark_shared)` replaces the flat override: same PP-safe early return, then delegate to the upstream check, then flag a successful share on the draft **only when the target is unrotated** (QuaRot builds a rotated private copy over the shared module in post_process, so flagging there would skip the rotation rebuild — including on PP=1, which was correct before this PR). The wrapper is installed per load by `_load_dspark_model_with_target_quant` with `mark_shared` derived from `get_rotation_path`, and restored afterwards. The `align_draft_weights` fallback itself is untouched and stays until the RFC PR 2 removal.
- `vllm_ascend/patch/__init__.py` — patch registry entry for the `maybe_share_target_embed` override (Why/How/Future Plan).

Behavior notes:

- GLM MoE DSA DSpark loads also flow through the wrapper: their existing target-side provisioning now keeps the shared shard instead of reloading it (same weights, one fewer load-time copy). Flagged here for visibility; the RFC PR 2 compatibility audit will re-verify.
- Known boundary: a GQA draft checkpoint that ships its own embedding keeps its own copy (correct); the provisioned shard then sits unconsumed — the predicate cannot see checkpoint contents at construction time.
- DeepSeek V4 same-checkpoint drafts are unchanged (no provisioning on that target; the wrapper early-return path is preserved).

The DSpark fallback removal stays in PR 2 (it requires the compatibility audit); the GLM5Next MTP migration is PR 3.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Kimi K3 with a DSpark draft without a checkpoint-owned embedding (e.g. the Qwen3 GQA draft) under PP>1 now reuses the target input embedding loaded on the last PP stage instead of reloading a private copy from the checkpoint during draft initialization; QuaRot targets keep the existing behavior. A release note fragment is included in this PR.

### How was this patch tested?

- Added `tests/ut/models/test_kimi_k3_target_embedding.py` (CPU-runnable):
  - provisioning scope matrix: PP=1/2/3 × draft architectures (`Qwen3DSparkModel`, `DSparkDraftModel`, `K3DSparkModel`, unknown) × no-spec / MTP;
  - real `VocabParallelEmbedding` + `weight_loader` TP sharding + sharing wrapper, asserting the draft aliases the same loaded module (RFC validation item 1);
  - rotated/unrotated end-to-end through the real `align_draft_weights`: unrotated keeps the shared module, QuaRot rebuilds `E @ R^T` (RFC QuaRot path);
  - `mark_shared` wiring: the load wrapper installs the share check with the flag derived from the target rotation state;
  - MLA draft keeps its own checkpoint embedding with no second target allocation;
  - a missing shared embedding fails the upstream check instead of silently passing (RFC validation item 2).
- Updated `tests/ut/models/test_kimi_k3_pp_sp.py` (AST extraction namespace additions for the new predicate).
- The predicate was additionally verified locally by extracting the function AST and exercising 14 branch combinations.
- **Pending before merge** (needs NPU hardware): RFC validation item 3 — real-weight Kimi K3 GQA DSpark at PP>1 (startup, greedy parity with target-only decoding, nonzero accepted draft tokens, per-TP-rank resident memory before/after and peak during loading, unrotated and QuaRot paths reported separately). Results will be reported in this PR.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: the provisioning scope matrix covers PP=1, middle stage, last stage, missing speculative config, non-dspark method, draft vocab exceeding the target, QuaRot targets, and unknown draft architectures.
- [ ] **Regression test**: not a bug fix; the new behavior is covered by the scope matrix above.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: `test_missing_shared_embedding_raises_without_provisioning` locks the fail-fast raise when a required shared embedding is unavailable.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: the loader test asserts numerically correct TP shards against hand-computed slices, the end-to-end test drives the real `align_draft_weights`, and the provisioned module is asserted to register as a real parameter — mirroring `test_deepseek_pp_embedding.py`.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: construction-time path only (one embedding allocation per last-stage TP rank when triggered); steady-state forward is untouched. Unrotated PP>1 additionally drops the duplicate shard allocation during draft loading. Per-RFC memory accounting is part of the pending NPU validation.

issues.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds e2e embedding test coverage and a user-facing tutorial for `intfloat/e5-mistral-7b-instruct` (7B embedding model, plain `MistralModel` without LM head, last-token pooling + L2 normalization), per #10679.

### Acceptance-criteria scoping (explicit, per #10679)

- **Configs yaml AND data exemption**: this PR delivers the executable pytest script and docs instead of a configs yaml. On the model side, the configs yaml has a single consumer, `test_lm_eval_correctness.py`, which only accepts lm-eval-generated tasks — an embedding (pooling) model has no valid model_type there, and there is no lm_eval precedent for embedding models. On the data side, the evaluation corpus is **40 fully self-constructed zh/en query-passage pairs** (no MS MARCO text redistribution — MS MARCO disallows redistribution, so no third-party data or download script is shipped; license noted in the test docstring). The repository also has dedicated consumers for non-lm-eval model types (`test_rm_eval_correctness.py` with `model_type=vllm-rm`, `test_asr_eval_correctness.py` with `vllm-asr`). Following that pattern (a new consumer + yaml, the #11364 shape) would require extending the shared harness; this PR keeps the change test-only and leaves such a consumer as a possible follow-up.

The exemption therefore covers both the "model config" and "data config" halves of the acceptance wording, stated here per the acceptance criteria of #10679.

### Prior art acknowledgment (#11364)

This work builds on the earlier draft PR #11364 — thanks to its authors for establishing the pooling-test direction on Ascend. Where the two overlap, this PR offers a more complete alternative, in the following ways:

- **Release note fragment**: adds `release_notes/fragments/19536.yaml` per the repository fragment convention (#11364 did not add one)
- **Support matrix row**: registers the model in `supported_models.md` (Pooling column, A2/A3) linking the tutorial
- **Stronger assertions**: element-wise |Δ| comparison after L2 normalization on both sides (catches a missing-normalization bug that cosine similarity cannot detect — cosine is norm-invariant), plus a 40-query top-1 ranking assertion where #11364 relied on looser similarity checks
- **Illegal-input cases**: empty string / whitespace-only / non-string inputs recorded per actual behavior (they do not error; they produce a BOS-only 4096-d vector on v0.26), non-string input explicitly rejected by the API
- **Scheduler A/B data**: full suite run under both `VLLM_ASCEND_BALANCE_SCHEDULING=1` and `=0` (and the `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` fallback path) with archived logs, demonstrating scheduler-independence of the results

### Why the pytest route instead of the #11364 yaml shape: #11364 demonstrated an alternative (yaml with model_type=vllm-embedding plus harness skip-logic changes and a new dedicated consumer), but that shape requires modifying the shared lm-eval harness (large blast radius for a test-only contribution) and has been stalled since July. This PR takes the route that PR CI can execute directly today; if maintainers prefer the #11364 shape, we are happy to merge efforts there.

_Note: the table above is produced by a separate measurement script over the 40 query-only texts (n=40); the committed pytest asserts the full query+passage set (n=80, shape (80, 4096)) with the same per-dimension criteria._

Test coverage (issue: embedding model correctness)

- 7 tests in `tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/pooling/test_e5_mistral_7b_instruct.py` (shape, numeric closeness, normalization, single-vs-batch consistency, top-1 ranking, token-id alignment, invalid inputs; pooling precedent location; one_card is routed to the a2-1 runner by test_config.yaml and runs in PR CI once a run-enabling label or an /e2e command is applied): shape, numeric closeness vs HF fp32 reference, top-1 ranking, token-id alignment (guards last-token misalignment; neither side auto-appends EOS), invalid inputs
- 40 self-constructed zh/en query-passage pairs (en=20, zh=20), asymmetric official template (`Instruct: {task}\nQuery: {q}` on the query side only, bare passages)
- Reference side: HF `AutoModel` fp32 + handwritten `last_token_pool` (left/right padding compatible) + L2 — no sentence-transformers dependency (version-drift free)

### Five-dimension evidence (set_env main path, custom op; bf16 vLLM vs fp32 HF, same NPU)

| Dimension | Metric | Measured | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shape | output == (40, 4096) | (40, 4096) | PASS |
| Numeric tolerance | element-wise \|Δ\| after L2 norm | max 0.006024, mean 0.000121 | PASS (tol 2e-2) |
| Normalization | L2 norm of raw vLLM output | 1.000000 (embed head hardcodes L2 on v0.26) | PASS |
| Cosine similarity | per-pair vLLM vs HF | min 0.999789, mean 0.999943 | PASS (tol 1e-3) |
| Ranking | top-1 agreement | 40/40 vLLM-vs-HF, 40/40 intended-pair hit on both sides | PASS |

### Environment & results

- vllm 0.26.0 / vllm-ascend 0.26.0rc1 / CANN 9.1.0 / torch_npu 2.10.0.post4 / Ascend 910, Ubuntu 22.04.5 (aarch64)
- Requires sourcing the vendor custom-op env before launch: `vllm_ascend/_cann_ops_custom/vendors/custom_transformer/bin/set_env.bash` (`ASCEND_CUSTOM_OPP_PATH` must be set before the vllm_ascend extension loads — documented in the tutorial)
- v0.26 API notes: CLI flag is `--pooler-config '{"pooling_type":"LAST"}'` (the old `--override-pooler-config` is renamed); the `PoolerConfig.normalize` field was removed — L2 is applied by the embedding pooler head by default, which the L2-norm evidence row above verifies
- Results: **7/7 passed** on the final head (~219 s); the earlier 5-test runs were 104.30 s / 102.22 s before the single-input case was added, `VLLM_ASCEND_BALANCE_SCHEDULING=1` (103.34s), `=0` (105.48s), and `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` fallback (102.76s); all within runtime noise of each other

### How was this patch tested?

- Local Ascend 910 (A2), single card, `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1`: full e2e suite `pytest -sv tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/pooling/test_e5_mistral_7b_instruct.py` → 6/6 passed (~122 s), plus the same suite under `VLLM_ASCEND_BALANCE_SCHEDULING=1` and `=0` (scheduler-independence), and under the `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` fallback path.
- Serving smoke + six curl observations against `/v1/embeddings` (shape 4096, L2 norm ~1.0, determinism, >4096 rejection, empty/whitespace behavior); screenshots are attached to #10679.
- CI: pre-commit (ruff, codespell, mypy on py3.10/3.11/3.12), cpu-ut, markdown-link, DCO are green. The e2e job is gated by a maintainer label (`ready-precise` / `ready-all` / `main2main`) or can be run by the `/e2e <path>` command.
### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes — it adds a user-facing model tutorial (`docs/source/tutorials/models/E5-Mistral-7B-Instruct.md`, registered in mkdocs nav) and registers the model in the pooling section of the support matrix. No runtime/API behavior changes. A release note fragment (`release_notes/fragments/19536.yaml`) is included per the repository convention.

### Checklist

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: added cases for empty string, whitespace-only, non-string input, and >4096-token rejection.
- [ ] **Regression test**: not applicable (no bug fix).
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: invalid / over-long inputs are asserted to raise the expected errors.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: five-dimension assertions (shape, element-wise tolerance after L2, normalization, cosine, top-1 ranking) against a Hugging Face fp32 reference.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: not applicable (test + docs only).
### Known CI status

(1) **vLLM main shard**: shared conftest import failure (`kv_cache_planning`), repo-wide, not this PR. (2) **vLLM v0.31.0**: the suite resolves weights offline and `intfloat/e5-mistral-7b-instruct` is not yet in `.github/workflows/misc/model_dataset_list.json`, so the first run failed on model lookup before any assertion; a maintainer needs `model-dataset-download`, then `ready-precise`. (3) Same `VLLMValidationError`/`ValueError` narrowing as the sibling PR, fixed on this branch.
Sister PR: #19531 (Qwen2.5-1.5B-apeach classification e2e).
Closes #10679
Related to #9079
